questions.question: With which of the following subjects are Article 123 and Article 213 of the Constitution of India associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ordinance-making power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 123**
 
• 
 According to article 123 in The Constitution Of India 1949, President has power to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament.

 
 
• If at any time, except when both Houses of Parliament are in session, the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action, he may promulgate such Ordinances as the circumstances appear to him to require.
 
• An Ordinance promulgated under this article shall have the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament, but every such Ordinance —(a) shall be laid before both Houses of Parliament and shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament, or, if before the expiration of that period resolutions disapproving it are passed by both Houses, upon the passing of the second of those resolutions; and(b) may be withdrawn at any time by the President.
 
• If and so far as an Ordinance under this article makes any provision which Parliament would not under this Constitution be competent to enact, it shall be void.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 213
 
• Article 213 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Governor of a state to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the state legislature. An ordinance is a temporary law that can be issued by the Governor when the legislative assembly or both houses of the legislature are not in session.

 Key points about Article 213:

 
• Power of Promulgation: The Governor has the authority to promulgate ordinances on matters that fall within the legislative competence of the state legislature.
 
• Circumstances for Promulgation: The Governor can issue ordinances when the state legislature is not in session, and the Governor believes that immediate action is required.
 
• Subject to Legislative Approval: Ordinances issued by the Governor are temporary in nature and need to be approved by the state legislature when it reconvenes. If not approved within a specified time, the ordinance ceases to operate.
 
• Limits on Ordinance Making: The power to issue ordinances is not absolute, and there are certain constitutional limitations. The Governor cannot promulgate ordinances on certain matters, including those reserved for the President, and there are restrictions on re-promulgation.

questions.question: What were cash crops such as cotton and sugarcane called during the Mughal period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jins-i-kamil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the Mughal Period, the land was divided into four categories namely
 
 
• Polaj - Which was cultivated every year.
 
• Parati - Which was sometimes left uncultivated for one or two years.
 
• Chachar - Which was left uncultivated for three or four years.
 
• Banjar - Which was left uncultivated for five years or more.
 
 
 
• Polaj was the land that is annually cultivated for each crop in succession and is never allowed to lie fallow.
 
• **Polaj** was the ideal and best type of** land throughout the empire.**
 
• This land was cultivated always and was **never allowed to lie fallow. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There was no **Mughal land revenue system **before **Akbar**.
 
• His father Humayun and grandfather Babur did not introduce any changes because they were the first conquerors of their dynasty and remained pre-occupied with subduing rebellions, consolidating empires, and maintaining order.
 
• A prope**r land revenue system **was founded by **Akbar**.
 
• However, the system of Akbar was itself based on what **Shershah Suri **implemented during his short tenure.
 
• Thus, the land revenue system of Akbar was neither innovation nor an invention.
 
• His indebtedness to the earlier rulers is immense but this has not diminished his fame as far as **the land revenue system **is concerned.
 
• He followed the policy of **Shershah** with greater precision and correctness and then extended it to various subah or provinces of his empire.
 
• But this correction or precision did not come overnight.
 
• Initially was tortuous enough to turn peasants into **beggars**, and forcing them to **sell their wives and children.**
 
• But it was revised several times.
 
• **The corrections done by the Akbar inland revenue system were as follows:**
 
 
• Standardization of measurement of land
 
• Ascertaining the produce per Bigha of Land
 
• Fixation of state’s share in that produce

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The flow of energy in the ecosystem is unidirectional.
The pyramid of energy is always inverted.
All ecosystems are stable in size.
In nature, only food chains exist, but not food webs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The flow of energy in the ecosystem is unidirectional.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Energy flow in an ecosystem starts from the sun and flows to producers, then to consumers, and finally to decomposers.
 
• This energy transfer follows a linear path and does not cycle back, making it unidirectional.
 
• At each trophic level, energy is lost primarily as heat due to metabolic processes.
 
• Only about 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, known as the 10% law of energy transfer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels**

 
 
• These are hierarchical levels in an ecosystem, comprising producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, and tertiary consumers.
 
• Producers (e.g., plants) generate energy through photosynthesis.
 
• Primary consumers (herbivores) eat producers.
 
• Secondary consumers (carnivores) eat primary consumers.
 
• Tertiary consumers are top predators that eat secondary consumers.
 
 
 
• **Food Chains and Food Webs**
 
 
• A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which nutrients and energy pass.
 
• Food webs consist of multiple interconnected food chains, providing a more accurate depiction of energy flow in ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Pyramid of Energy**
 
 
• This ecological pyramid shows the energy content at each trophic level.
 
• It is always upright, indicating the loss of energy at each trophic level.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a quality/feature of the parliamentary form of government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Single executive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The modern concept of parliamentary government emerged in the Kingdom of Great Britain between 1707 and 1800 and its contemporary, the Parliamentary System in Sweden between 1721 and 1772.
 
• Parliamentary System of Government
 
 
• There are two executives:
 
 
• The nominal executive is the head of state e.g. President while the real executive is the Prime Minister, who is the head of government.
 
 
 
• In such a system, the role of the president or monarch is primarily ceremonial and the Prime Minister along with the cabinet wields effective power.
 
• Countries with such a system include Germany, Italy, Japan, United Kingdom as well as Portugal.
 
• The Constitution of India provides for a parliamentary form of government, both at the Centre and in the States.
 
 
• Articles 74 and 75 deal with the parliamentary system of government at the Union level and Articles 163 and 164 contain provisions with regard to the States.
 
 
 
• The executive is responsible to the legislature for its policies and acts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Presidential System of Government

 
 
• There is only one executive.
 
• In this system, the President is both head of state and government, e.g. the USA, South Korea etc.
 
• The executive is not responsible to the legislature for its policies and acts and is constitutionally independent of the legislature in respect of its term of office.

• **Anti-cyclone**

 
 
• An anti-cyclone is a large-scale circulation of winds around a central region of high atmospheric pressure.
 
• In the Northern Hemisphere, winds in an anticyclone circulate clockwise, while in the Southern Hemisphere, they circulate counterclockwise.
 
• Anticyclones are associated with fair weather conditions, such as clear skies, light winds, and little precipitation.
 
• They form due to the sinking of cool air, which increases air pressure at the surface.
 
• Anticyclones can influence weather patterns over large areas, often leading to prolonged periods of stable weather.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convection**

 
 
• In meteorology, convection refers to the vertical movement of air due to differences in temperature and density.
 
• Warm air, being less dense, rises, while cooler air sinks.
 
• Convection plays a crucial role in driving weather patterns, such as thunderstorms and sea breezes.
 
• It is a fundamental process in the Earth's atmosphere, influencing the distribution of heat and moisture.
 
• Convection currents can also occur in other fluids, such as water and molten rock.
 
 
 
• **Cyclone**
 
 
• A cyclone is a large-scale atmospheric circulation characterized by low atmospheric pressure at its center.
 
• In the Northern Hemisphere, winds in a cyclone circulate counterclockwise, while in the Southern Hemisphere, they circulate clockwise.
 
• Cyclones are associated with stormy weather conditions, including strong winds, heavy rain, and sometimes tornadoes.
 
• They form due to the rising of warm, moist air, which creates an area of low pressure.
 
• Tropical cyclones, hurricanes, and typhoons are all types of cyclones.
 
 
 
• **Orography**
 
 
• Orography refers to the influence of topography, such as mountains and hills, on weather patterns.
 
• When air masses encounter a mountain range, they are forced to rise, which can lead to cooling and condensation, resulting in precipitation.
 
• This phenomenon is known as orographic lifting.
 
• Orography can significantly impact regional climates, creating rain shadows on the leeward side of mountain ranges and influencing the distribution of precipitation.
 
• The Himalayas, for example, create a rain shadow effect on the Tibetan Plateau.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitar**__.

Sitar instrument:

__
 
• The sitar is a plucked stringed instrument, originating from the Indian subcontinent, used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• The instrument was invented in medieval India and flourished in the 16th and 17th centuries and arrived at its present form in 18th-century India.
 
• Used widely throughout the Indian subcontinent, the sitar became popularly known in the wider world through the works of Ravi Shankar, beginning in the late 1950s and early 1960s.
 
• In the 1960s, a short-lived trend arose for the use of the sitar in Western popular music, with the instrument appearing on tracks by bands such as the Beatles, the Doors, the Rolling Stones, and others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santoor**

 
 
• The santoor is a hammered dulcimer, a trapezoid-shaped instrument with strings that are struck with small mallets.
 
• It has its origins in Persia and is a popular instrument in Indian classical music, particularly in the Kashmir region.
 
• The santoor typically has 100 strings arranged in groups, and the player uses two small wooden mallets to produce a wide range of sounds and effects.
 
• It is known for its delicate and expressive sound, capable of producing both subtle and powerful musical phrases.
 
• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was a renowned santoor virtuoso who played a crucial role in popularizing the instrument in Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Sarod**
 
 
• The sarod is a fretless, long-necked lute that is a prominent instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is characterized by its deep, resonant sound and intricate playing techniques.
 
• The sarod has a gourd-shaped body and a long neck with 20 to 25 frets.
 
• It is played with a small metal plectrum called a "meend" that allows for subtle variations in pitch and timbre.
 
• Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Ustad Amjad Ali Khan are two of the most celebrated sarod maestros in the world.
 
 
 
• **Violin**
 
 
• The violin is a string instrument with four strings, played with a bow.
 
• It is one of the most widely recognized and versatile instruments in Western classical music.
 
• The violin has a long history, evolving from earlier bowed instruments like the viol.
 
• It is capable of producing a wide range of sounds, from delicate and lyrical to powerful and dramatic.
 
• Famous violinists include Niccolò Paganini, Jascha Heifetz, and Itzhak Perlman.
